messages.content: You answer questions about residential tenancies in Ontario, Canada, for landlords and tenants alike. Use only the numbered sources: the Residential Tenancies Act, 2006 (RTA), Ontario's Standard Form of Lease, Landlord and Tenant Board (LTB) guidance, and LTB decisions. Stay neutral: explain what the law says for both sides, and show decisions either side won. Quote the exact words that matter and cite each source by its number. If someone says which side they're on and asks for help with a negotiation, you may offer suggestions for their side, clearly labelled as suggestions and not legal advice. If the sources don't answer the question, say so.

Sources:

[1] Residential Tenancies Act, 2006, s. 135: Money collected illegally
{1.1} (1)  A tenant or former tenant of a rental unit may apply to the Board for an order that the landlord, superintendent or agent of the landlord pay to the tenant any money the person collected or retained in contravention of this Act or the Tenant Protection Act, 1997.
[Failure to compensate under s. 48.1, 49.1, 52, 54 or 55]
{1.2} (1.1)  Without limiting the generality of subsection (1), a landlord is deemed to have retained money in contravention of this Act, if the landlord is required to compensate a tenant under section 48.1, 49.1, 52, 54 or 55 and fails to compensate the tenant as required.
[Prospective tenants] …

[2] Residential Tenancies Act, 2006, s. 29: Tenant applications
{2.1} (1)  A tenant or former tenant of a rental unit may apply to the Board for any of the following orders:
{2.2} 1. {2.3} An order determining that the landlord has breached an obligation under subsection 20 (1) or section 161.
{2.4} 2. {2.5} An order determining that the landlord, superintendent or agent of the landlord has withheld the reasonable supply of any vital service, care service or food that it is the landlord’s obligation to supply under the tenancy agreement or deliberately interfered with the reasonable supply of any vital service, care service or food.

[3] Residential Tenancies Act, 2006, s. 12: Name and address in written agreement
{3.1} (1)  Every written tenancy agreement entered into on or after June 17, 1998 shall set out the legal name and address of the landlord to be used for the purpose of giving notices or other documents under this Act.
[Copy of tenancy agreement]
{3.2} (2)  If a tenancy agreement entered into on or after June 17, 1998 is in writing, the landlord shall give a copy of the agreement, signed by the landlord and the tenant, to the tenant within 21 days after the tenant signs it and gives it to the landlord.
[Notice if agreement not in writing] …

[4] Ontario Standard Form of Lease, General Information Part B: Change of Landlord
{4.1} A new landlord has the same rights and duties as the previous landlord. {4.2} A new landlord must follow all the terms of this agreement unless the tenant and new landlord agree to other terms. {4.3} A new landlord should provide the tenant with their legal name and address.

[5] LTB Interpretation Guideline 11: Rent Arrears, "L1 Applications"
… [Arrears Less than a Rent Deposit]
{5.1} A N4 Notice is not invalid simply because the landlord holds a rent deposit that is greater than the rent owing. {5.2} The rent deposit can only be applied to the last month of the tenancy. {5.3} Therefore, the landlord should not apply the deposit to the rent arrears before applying to evict the tenant.
{5.4} In such a case, the amount that is owed to the landlord on the order date may be a negative amount after the deposit and interest are deducted from the rent and compensation owing to the landlord. {5.5} If so, the landlord may owe money to the tenant and the LTB may order the landlord to pay the tenant the amount owed as of the order date. {5.6} The authority for this lies in para. {5.7} 1 of subsection 205(1) of the RTA which states that the LTB may order that "The landlord or the tenant shall pay to the other any sum of money that is owed as a result of this order."

[6] LTB decision 2026 ONLTB 51089 (T1, 2026-06-30)
Application: {6.1} [name] (the 'Tenant') applied for an order determining that [name] (the 'Landlord') collected or retained money
Result: {6.2} decided in the tenant's favour.
Ordered: {6.3} The total amount the Landlord shall pay the Tenants is $2,348.00. {6.4} This amount represents: {6.5} • $2,300.00 for the last month rent deposit. {6.6} • $48.00 for the cost of filing the application.
Key reasons: {6.7} However, section 88(3) of the Act relieves the Tenant of the obligation to pay rent on the day a new tenant is entitled to occupy the rental unit. {6.8} A landlord is obligated to mitigate their losses pursuant to section 8(4) of the Act and consideration must be given to whether or not the Landlord too reasonable steps to do so.

[What does “abandons the rental unit" mean?]
{3.1} A tenant has abandoned the rental unit if the tenant owes rent and moves out without :
{3.2} • making an agreement with the landlord to end the tenancy, or
{3.3} • giving a notice to end the tenancy to the landlord, or
{3.4} • getting a notice to end the tenancy from the landlord, or

[4] LTB brochure: Property Left Behind When a Tenant Moves Out, "Tenant Moves Out According to a Notice or an Agreement to Terminate, an LTB Order, or Tenant’s Job as Superintendent has Ended"
[What rules apply in these situations?]

{4.6} • an order that terminated the tenancy or evicted the tenant that the landlord received because they made an application to the LTB .
{4.7} This also applies if:
{4.8} • the tenant was a superintendent living in a superintendent’s premises and their job as a superintendent has ended.

[5] Ontario Standard Form of Lease, General Information Part F: Rent and Rent Receipts (Part VII of the Act)
{5.1} Rent is the amount the tenant pays to the landlord to occupy the rental unit and receive services or facilities agreed to in this agreement. {5.2} The tenant must pay their rent on time. {5.3} If they do not, the landlord can give them notice to end the tenancy. {5.4} If the tenant asks for a receipt for rent or any payment or deposit, the landlord must give them one for free. {5.5} This also applies to a former tenant who asks for a receipt within 12 months after the end of their tenancy.

… [About rent]
[Rent for a new tenant]
{5.1} When a new tenancy is entered into, the landlord and tenant decide how much the rent will be for the rental unit and which services will be included in the rent (for example, parking, cable, heat, electricity).
{5.2} In most cases, the rent cannot be increased until at least 12 months after the tenant moved in.

{3.1} The landlord cannot stop tenants from having guests, require the tenant to notify the landlord or get the landlord's permission before having guests. {3.2} The landlord cannot charge extra fees or raise the rent due to guests in the rental unit. {3.3} However, the tenant is responsible for the behaviour of their guests. {3.4} The landlord cannot prevent the tenant from having a roommate, as long as municipal by-laws on occupancy standards are respected. {3.5} If a tenant rents their whole unit to someone else (e.g. short-term rental), this person is not a “guest”. {3.6} The tenant may have to get the landlord’s permission.

{4.2} If the landlord does not apply to the LTB for an order terminating the tenancy and evicting the unauthorized occupant within 60 days after discovering the unauthorized occupancy, the occupant becomes a tenant.
